occurrences.quote: Was the town of Antelope, Kansas (in Centre USD 397 district) named after the pronghorn (Antilocapra americana)? What is the historical origin of the name "Antelope" for this town?

Does Passage [7] (or any other passage) explicitly state that the town of Antelope was named after antelope or Antilocapra americana grazing in the area, or is the connection between the town's name and this species based on inference from the town being in antelope habitat?

Grazing antelope | A grazing antelope is any of the species of antelope that make up the subfamily Hippotraginae of the family Bovidae.  As grazers, rather than browsers, the "Hippo" in Hippotraginae refers to the slightly horse-like characteristics of body size and proportions: long legs and a solid body with a relatively thick muscular neck.
Antelope Creek Phase | The Antelope Creek Phase was an American Indian culture in the Texas Panhandle and adjacent Oklahoma dating from 1200 to 1450 AD.
